key_insight: Competing Ge-driven polar off-centering and Sn-favored octahedral tilting create a low-temperature phase boundary at x = 0.60–0.65 in lead-free CsGe₁₋ₓSnₓBr₃ alloys.
engineering_relevance: Ge/Sn composition offers a route to tune polar order, crystal structure, and band gap in lead-free halide perovskites.
method: Train a charge-aware machine-learned interatomic potential on hybrid-functional data.
Run large-scale molecular dynamics across the full Ge/Sn composition range.
Map temperature-dependent tilting, off-centering, and structural phases.
evidence_signal: Simulations reproduce known transition sequences and temperatures of both end members and predict an intermediate tetragonal I4/mcm phase absent from either parent compound.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation-based alloy predictions; experimental validation of the phase boundary and intermediate phase remains necessary.
paper_title: Competing Octahedral Tilting and $B$-Site Off-Centering Govern the Phase Diagram of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ Perovskite Alloys
